auditedPages.note: Applied the LOW_INFORMATION_GAIN test (Part 5) to the 15 Tier-A pages already researched in Phase IV: does the page provide anything beyond a vendor-feature summary (seat math, pricing thresholds, migration guidance, buyer-specific tradeoffs)?

findings.reason: Zero cons documented; pricing is 'contact sales' with no structured detail beyond that. The page currently only lists features and a generic alternatives comparison -- no buyer-decision logic.

Has real, structured tiered pricing (Free/Starter EUR45/Standard EUR280/Professional EUR730/Enterprise custom) and a genuine differentiator (.NET vs PHP), but no seat-math or migration-specific guidance.

findings.page: most other Tier-A pages (clickup, salesforce, confluence, n8n, basecamp, tidio, zapier, github, activecampaign, segment, lastpass, webex, coda)
findings.reason: All are fd=A (real pricing tiers, real cons, real sourced features) -- genuinely more complete than a bare vendor summary -- but none currently include seat-math, plan-gate-specific buyer logic, or a migration checklist. They answer 'what does this cost and what are its limits' but not 'at what point does this specific constraint bind for MY team.'

overallVerdict: Most researched pages sit at MODERATE information gain: real, sourced, structured facts (a genuine step above a vendor's own marketing page or a thin listicle entry) but not yet the kind of buyer-specific decision logic (seat-math thresholds, migration checklists, 'test this during your trial') that would make Miloosh's pages genuinely irreplaceable rather than merely well-sourced.
part6_realInformationGainBuilt: Not executed this session as a new page feature -- see changes.md for reasoning.
